description: Modify order_filled ingestion to support incremental fetching — only fetch records newer than the last known timestamp instead of re-fetching the entire day
steps: Add helper function to find the latest timestamp from existing order_filled data in S3 (read latest manifest, check for latest_timestamp in source metadata)
Add fallback: if manifest has no latest_timestamp field, download the latest data file and scan for max timestamp value
Modify ingest_order_filled() to accept optional since_timestamp parameter
When since_timestamp is provided, use timestamp_gte=since_timestamp in Goldsky query instead of day boundaries
Write latest_timestamp into manifest source metadata on each run (max timestamp from fetched records)
Preserve backwards compatibility: without since_timestamp, existing full-day behavior is unchanged
Add unit tests for incremental fetch path (since_timestamp passed to GoldskyClient, manifest includes latest_timestamp)

description: Build S3 scanning logic to find the most recent timestamp for a given platform/entity, used by both incremental ingestion and the catchup command
steps: Create async helper function: find_latest_timestamp(s3_client, bucket, platform, entity) -> int | None
List S3 prefixes under bronze/{platform}/{entity}/ to discover all dt= date partitions
Extract dates from key paths via regex, find the latest date
Within the latest date, find the latest run_id directory (by manifest generated_at timestamp)
Read the manifest: if source.latest_timestamp exists, return it
Fallback: download the data file (part-000.jsonl.gz), decompress, scan for max timestamp field, return it
Return None if no data exists at all
Add unit tests: manifest with latest_timestamp field, manifest without field (data scan fallback), no data exists, multiple dates/runs

description: Add 'prediction-data backfill catchup' CLI command that auto-detects the latest data and catches up to present
steps: Add catchup command to backfill_app in cli/main.py with options: --platform, --entity, --bucket, --dry-run
Resolve platform/entity filters using existing _resolve_platforms() and _resolve_entities() helpers
For order_filled: call find_latest_timestamp(), then run incremental ingest_order_filled(since_timestamp=latest_ts)
For other date-scoped entities (trades): find latest date in S3, backfill missing days to today using existing _run_backfill()
For catalog entities (markets, events): find latest date, run fresh snapshot for today if not already present
In --dry-run mode: print what would be fetched (latest timestamp found, time range to fetch, entities to process) without executing
Log 'already up to date' and skip if no new data is expected
Log 'no existing data found' and skip if platform/entity has never been ingested (user should run initial backfill first)
Continue on failure per entity, collect errors, report summary and exit non-zero if any failures

description: Add comprehensive tests for incremental ingestion and catchup command
steps: Add unit tests for find_latest_timestamp() with mocked S3Client (manifest with field, fallback scan, no data, multiple dates)
Add unit tests for catchup command: dry-run output, incremental path for order_filled, full-day path for trades, catalog path for markets/events
Add unit tests for edge cases: no existing data (skip), already up to date (skip), failure continues to next entity
Add unit tests for incremental ingest_order_filled (since_timestamp forwarded to Goldsky, latest_timestamp written to manifest)
Ensure all tests pass: pytest -m 'not integration'
Ensure type checking passes: mypy src/
Ensure linting passes: ruff check src/ tests/

description: Update project documentation with catchup command and incremental ingestion model
steps: Update CLAUDE.md: add catchup CLI examples to Backfill CLI section, add note about incremental order_filled ingestion
Update RELEASE.md: add catchup command to CLI contract (section 9), document incremental ingestion model for order_filled
Update FORBRIAN.md: add Sprint 10 section explaining incremental ingestion design, catchup command, and lessons learned
